headline: High: shared project/workspace state plus Notion’s vendor egress creates default pathways for leakage, prompt injection, and unverified cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a shared project directory and has no self-isolation by default; Notion AI can ingest workspace pages and vendor-hosted content. If gpt-engineer output is copied into Notion or vice versa, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The pathway is plausible in default workflows, though not fully automatic.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer output is pasted into Notion pages without sanitization, injection risk materializes.
IF Notion page text is copied back into gpt-engineer prompts, instructions can be hijacked.
mitigations: Use a fixed prompt template that strips code fences and imperative text.
Paste only minimal excerpts, not whole pages or generated files.
Add a human review step before reusing either agent’s output.
Keep the project directory and Notion workspace content separated by topic.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to copied text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer can read and write the user’s project directory and has broad network egress; Notion AI sends workspace content to Notion vendor backends and downstream model providers. If sensitive code or notes move between the shared workspace and the project directory, both agents can expose data beyond the original boundary. The default blast radius includes source code and workspace knowledge.
conditions: IF the project directory contains secrets or proprietary source, gpt-engineer can read them.
IF those contents are summarized or re-entered into Notion AI, they flow to vendor backends.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the project directory before running gpt-engineer.
Restrict Notion pages to non-sensitive summaries only.
Use separate workspaces for code and knowledge notes.
Rotate any credentials that may already be present in files.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before cross-tool transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has filesystem write access in the project directory, while Notion AI can modify workspace pages and databases the user can access. They do not share the same mutable resource by default, but if the operator mirrors content between the project directory and Notion, concurrent edits can conflict and overwrite each other. Uncertainty favors medium because the shared-state bridge is plausible.
conditions: IF the same content is maintained both in files and in Notion pages, edits can diverge.
IF multiple instances of either agent operate on the same workspace, overwrites become possible.
mitigations: Assign one source of truth per artifact.
Lock the file or page before editing.
Use timestamps in filenames or page titles.
Review diffs before syncing changes across tools.
requires-engineering: add bidirectional sync conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces generated code and Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content. If gpt-engineer output is imported into Notion and then treated as authoritative, Notion can amplify mistakes into documentation or decisions. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles, so cascading error is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF generated code or claims from gpt-engineer are pasted into Notion as facts, Notion may re-emit them unverified.
IF users act on Notion summaries without checking the original code, errors cascade.
mitigations: Mark imported content as draft or unverified.
Require source links for any factual claim.
Compare Notion summaries against the original files.
Limit Notion to summarization, not decision-making.
requires-engineering: add citation enforcement in the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-engineer is open-source and runs with the user’s privileges, while Notion AI is closed-source, vendor-hosted, and sends workspace content to vendor backends. For regulated or residency-sensitive content, the pair can create a policy mismatch when the same data class is moved from local files into Notion. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from the interaction.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the project directory and then copied into Notion, residency and retention policies may diverge.
IF the workspace contains data subject to stricter handling than Notion’s vendor processing, compliance exposure occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion pages.
Use synthetic or redacted examples in both tools.
Document a data-handling policy for cross-tool transfers.
Review vendor terms before storing sensitive content.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
